newsitem.title: USA: Ecopetrol awards Cusiana cargo to U.S. refiner.
newsitem.headline: Ecopetrol awards Cusiana cargo to U.S. refiner.

text.p: Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol awarded a cargo of Cusiana crude oil to a U.S. refiner for loading June 23-24, trade sources said on Wednesday.
The buyer paid a discount of between $1.30 and $1.40 a barrel to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for the cargo of 550,000 barrels, the sources said.
"It's a distressed cargo, so does this redefine the Cusiana market? Probably not," one trader noted.
The sale marks Ecopetrol's second attempt to sell this cargo. The company last week decided to cancel a tender for the same cargo for loading June 17-18 after failing to receive acceptable bids.
Ecopetrol then shifted the loading dates to June 23-24 in an effort to spur more interest.
The gasoline-rich grade was last sold into the Gulf Coast for a discount of around $1.23 to WTI/Cushing.
The recent softening in part reflects firmer Caribbean freight rates, traders said.
Equity producer Total SA has the next Cusiana cargo loading at the end of June to early July.

Current Cusiana production of around 180,000 barrels per day (bpd) is slated to increase to 500,000 bpd by the end of 1997. Loadings are expected to begin rising in the third quarter, trade sources said.
